title: Choose the visual world for Booster Rocket
question: The roll assigned Case Tag. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Sketches show the parent home on a phone.

options.label: Case Tag
options.lineage: instrument-case, uniform and claim-check tags in a band hall
options.thesis: Each student is a tag hung on their gear: name, part, number, and what's still to do.
options.viewport: Club bar, family total with Pay, then one hanging tag per student whose finished forms are punched through.
options.risk: The tag notch and grommet turn cute if overdrawn; they must stay one quiet shape.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale: the family total and student names lead by size, not by boxes.
One state vocabulary: to do, waiting, done and closed drawn the same on every screen.
One fixed urgency ramp for money: paid, due, due soon, past due, never ad-hoc colour.
Totals that add up on the page: tabular figures, right-aligned, the total visibly the sum.
Tap a tag and it opens its items while the other tags stay folded.

options.label: Dot Book
options.lineage: marching-band drill charts and the dot books students wear on lanyards
options.thesis: The season as a drill: every family moves through numbered sets, and the next set is always marked.
options.viewport: A yard-line ruler of the season's sets across the top, current set highlighted, students and their next step below.
options.risk: The obvious marching-band reference, and it means nothing to concert, theatre or sports booster clubs.

options.label: Next-Step Bands
options.thesis: Home shows only the decisions ahead, as full-width signs in the club colour; done things drop off.
options.viewport: Stacked bands such as '2 forms left for Maya' and '$185.00 to pay', each with a big count and an arrow.
options.case: Fuses cleanly, since the parent home is a chain of next steps; loses on identification, as parents don't see their club in an airport.
options.risk: A pale or very dark club colour breaks the band contrast unless the theme adjusts it.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: The family total as a giant live specimen.
options.viewport: One enormous figure with tiny labels.
options.risk: Pure type show; no parent recognises it.
options.case: Loses both axes: no identification, and money as spectacle.

options.label: Reference Setting
options.lineage: scholarly editions with a centre rail
options.thesis: Family records set like an annotated edition.
options.viewport: Two narrow columns round a rail of keys.
options.risk: Scholarly and dense; wrong for a phone in a pickup line.
options.case: Loses both axes: too dense and too bookish.
options.kept: States as one consistent set of printed marks.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Students as stars ranked by what's left to do.
options.viewport: A dark chart with ranked dots.
options.risk: Dark, abstract, and poetic about money.
options.case: Loses both axes: abstract where parents need plain facts.
options.kept: Importance on one fixed, ordered ramp.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Each season as a side A / side B tracklist.
options.viewport: A folded card with timed rows.
options.risk: Handwriting costume; nostalgic, not trustworthy for money.
options.case: Loses both axes: parents don't map invoices to tracklists.
options.kept: Running totals right-aligned and made to add up exactly.

options.label: Title-Card Wall
options.thesis: Students and forms as poster rows.
options.risk: Entertainment shell; hides money and forms behind browsing.
options.case: Loses both axes: browsing is the wrong job.
options.kept: The focused item expands while the rest stay compact.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean school-app home: club header, a balance card, a forms card, a students list.
canonCard.viewport: Header with logo, then stacked cards for balance, forms and students.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other parent app by design.
